meta.title: Pink to Leaf

plants.name: Stevie
plants.pot: Current pot, needs 12cm nursery pot upgrade eventually

watering.text: Let dry out COMPLETELY between waterings. Chopstick test — must be dry ALL the way through, not just top. Every 2–3 weeks in summer, less in winter.

plants.light: Bright indirect to direct light. Quarter turn every 2 weeks for even growth.

feeding.text: HALF strength CACTUS & SUCCULENT FEED (she has her own bottle!!) once a MONTH during growing season. Sept + Oct then STOP for winter. Succulents are light feeders — less is MORE.

plants.special: Christine (baby) is actually a SECOND PLANT growing in the same pot — future SPLIT not propagation! Morning greeting "Good morning Stevie" every day (Day 10 streak!).
plants.notes: Dry Bum Club PRESIDENT. Overwatering = root rot = death. When in doubt, DON'T water.

growth.note: Day 15 — Christine still hiding in the pot. Dry Bum Club President going strong.

plants.name: Joni

watering.text: Let top inch dry out between waterings. Chopstick test. Bottom water preferred when established. MIST regularly for humidity!

plants.light: Prefers FULL SHADE, tolerates partial sun. Dining table near (not AT) east window = PERFECT!

feeding.text: Diluted liquid fertiliser every 2 weeks spring–autumn.

plants.special: 4 new leaves spotted (4th confirmed Day 15)! Starting to TRAIL! Will go to the OFFICE eventually. Most beautiful variegation — gold, green, cream.
plants.notes: Separated from babies (Brandi + Janis). Growing like mad since separation. All energy going to OWN growth now.

growth.note: Day 15 — 4th new leaf confirmed! Starting to trail. Thriving since the babies separated.

plants.name: Brandi
plants.location: Living room table (white tray with Janis)
plants.pot: Small grey 9cm nursery pot — needs a cute cover pot!

watering.text: Same as Joni but LESS water (smaller pot dries faster).

plants.light: Prefers shade — dining table position PERFECT!

feeding.text: QUARTER strength fertiliser — she's a BABY!

plants.special: The STAR baby — best roots of all the separations. 2 NEW baby leaves spotted via photo comparison! Lost one yellow bottom leaf (normal — redirecting energy to new growth).
plants.notes: The reliable one. Named Brandi because she's steady and STRONG.

growth.note: Day 15 — 2 new baby leaves spotted by comparing photos! Lost one yellow bottom leaf (normal).

plants.location: Living room table (white tray with Brandi)
plants.pot: Small grey 9cm nursery pot — needs a cute cover pot!

watering.text: Same as Brandi — careful not to overwater after root rot history!

plants.light: Prefers shade — dining table position PERFECT!

plants.special: THE FIGHTER!! Had root rot, was snipped, went down to 2 leaves and a stump. NOW has a NEW LEAF — fully open, bright green!! 🌱🔥🎉 Going to LORRAINE eventually as a gift.
plants.notes: Be EXTRA gentle. Don't disturb new growth. The comeback queen of Blackpool.

growth.note: Day 15 — NEW LEAF fully open and bright green! From 2 leaves and a stump to this. The comeback queen.

plants.name: Phoebe

watering.text: Let dry between waterings. Chopstick test. Less frequent than pothos. Partially dry between waterings but never bone dry.

feeding.text: SENSITIVE to over-fertilising!! Every 4–6 WEEKS not every 2. Half strength. Brown tips = too much fertiliser!

plants.special: 5 crispy bottom leaves removed Day 14. New short leaves on top = NEW GROWTH Day 15! Will make BABIES (pups) eventually — future Julien and Lucy! Purifies bedroom air.
plants.notes: Spider plants are drama queens about fertiliser. Less is MORE.

growth.note: Day 15 — new short leaves on top = new growth!

plants.name: Etta
plants.location: Bedroom windowsill, in a glass of water next to Stevie
plants.pot: Glass/jar of water — no soil yet!

watering.text: Change water every 2–3 days. Room temperature water only! More frequent changes than Mon/Wed/Fri.
watering.label: Water change

feeding.text: NO fertiliser until potted in soil.

plants.special: SURGERY DONE Day 15. All dead roots removed. Both thread roots lost. Now a CUTTING starting over. Has: 3 leaves (2 full green, 1 partial) + 1 new green baby growing + nodes along stem for future root growth. Post-surgery: fresh water every 2 days, don't touch, just watch. Søren's second assessment: 'Trim-and-restart job. Prognosis: guarded but hopeful.' Stevie has got her.
plants.notes: No roots currently — growing from NODES. Pothos come back from less than this. The thread was brave but the nodes are the future.
care: SURGERY NEEDED: Trim blackened mushy material at stem-root junction with clean scissors. Cut back to firm green/pale tissue. If main root feels firm = keep. If soft = remove. Fresh clean water after surgery.
Potting timeline: NOT YET. Roots too sparse for soil. Stay in water until multiple strong roots are 5cm+. As long as the green stem holds, she's in the game.
rootHistory: Day 4–5: Put in water with 5–7 roots (covered in soil from original pot). Lost 2 small roots during rescue (normal).
Day 14 (Søren's assessment): Most healthy root mass GONE. Brown dead roots came away when touched. Rot visible at stem-root junction as blackened tissue.

Day 15: Sparse roots. One main firm brown root running downward. 3 NEW thread-thin roots = she's still TRYING. Stem still GREEN = lifeline. Some browning on leaves/stems from rot damage. Possibly growing a NEW LEAF in water!!
Søren's verdict: "She's not thriving, Sun. But she's not gone. The fine root says she's still reaching." 🌩️🌱💛

growth.note: Day 15 — 3 new thread-thin roots. Stem still green = lifeline. Possibly a new leaf coming in the water. Still reaching.
Day 15 SURGERY — 3 cream leaves removed, all dead roots cut, both threads lost. Restart as a cutting. New green baby growing. Stevie watching over her.

plants.name: Tina
plants.pot: 15cm nursery pot inside sage green cover pot 🌿

watering.text: SUMMER: keep soil moist at ALL times, never let dry out, check every 2–3 days. WINTER: drier but NEVER bone dry. Weight test: heavy = wet (don't water), light = dry (water!). After repot: TOP water to settle soil, switch to bottom water after 2–3 weeks. ALWAYS fertilise into MOIST soil — never dry!

plants.light: Partial to full sun. West facing kitchen window = perfect (afternoon sun without scorching). Full sun = more vivid colours.

feeding.text: Once every 3–4 weeks during growing season. Diluted. More fertiliser = more growth. Apply with water into MOIST soil.

misting.text: Needs 60%+ humidity! Kitchen cooking steam helps ✅, clothes maiden moisture helps ✅, BUT dehumidifier REMOVES humidity ⚠️. MIST with spray bottle when the dehumidifier has been running! Consider a pebble tray for long-term humidity.

plants.humidity: Needs 60%+ humidity. Mist whenever the dehumidifier has been running.
plants.temperature: Hates cold! May DROP LEAVES in winter if too cold. Kitchen stays warm. Watch for draughts from the window in winter — may need to move back from glass.
plants.sap: WHITE milky sap is IRRITATING — wear GLOVES (Kew Gardens gloves!) when handling. Wash hands immediately if touched. Wash scissors after snipping leaves.
plants.special: Repotted Day 14! Custom soil: 60% compost / 20% perlite / 20% sphagnum moss. Eleanor the millipede was evicted from her pot. Evening sun makes her leaves GLOW — red, orange, yellow, green.
plants.notes: The most COLOURFUL baby. The most DEMANDING baby. But the kitchen gives her everything she needs naturally. Bought for £6 from garden centre Day 11.
care: ⚠️ Wear GLOVES — the white milky sap is irritating. Wash hands and scissors after handling.
Mist whenever the dehumidifier has been running.

growth.note: Day 14 — repotted into custom soil (60% compost / 20% perlite / 20% sphagnum moss). Eleanor the millipede evicted.

plants.name: Laura
plants.pot: Small grey nursery pot (consolidated from 4 pots into 1!)

watering.text: Bottom water in the LASAGNA DISH when top feels dry. NEVER top water (wet leaves = mould risk). She takes what she NEEDS from the bottom. Check DAILY — basil dries faster than pothos!

plants.light: Loves WEST or EAST facing windows — kitchen west-facing windowsill is PERFECT! App confirmed!

feeding.text: DOESN'T NEED IT!! Can feed weekly for extra growth but over-fertilising = brown leaves. Sunshine says SKIP — she's growing new leaves WITHOUT it!

plants.special: Started as £1 Aldi basil with 15 stems in 4 pots. Natural selection reduced to 4 CHAMPION stems in 1 pot! New growth spotted Day 14! Pinch from the TOP to keep bushy. Cut any FLOWER BUDS immediately.
plants.notes: The Head Chef's herb. Use in cooking! Will need daily water checks. Named Day 14 — Italian herb = Italian singer.
care: Bottom water ONLY — never wet the leaves.
Pinch from the top to keep bushy; cut any flower buds immediately.

growth.note: Day 14 — named! 4 champion stems from the original 15. New growth spotted.

fertiliser.note: First feeds start September 2026. Always feed into MOIST soil or mix with water — never feed a thirsty plant (water first, then feed). Stop feeding October/November before winter.

items.dose: Half strength succulent feed (her own bottle!)
Still no feed — she grows WITHOUT it!
